entities.summary:
New Line Cinema is an American film studio founded in 1967 by Robert Shaye as an independent distributor of 'B movies' and exploitation films, which grew into a major Hollywood studio best known for producing the Lord of the Rings trilogy (2001-2003), the Nightmare on Elm Street franchise (1984-1994), and the Austin Powers series. New Line was acquired by Time Warner in 1996 but continued as an independent unit; it was merged into Warner Bros. in 2008 after the costly Golden Compass (2007) failure.

New Line's transformation from grindhouse distributor to major studio came through Robert Shaye's shrewd risk-taking: the 1984 production of Nightmare on Elm Street for $1.8 million that grossed $25 million (creating Freddy Krueger as a cultural icon) established New Line as a viable independent. The nickname 'The House That Freddy Built' reflected how the Nightmare franchise's consistent profitability funded New Line's growth.

Peter Jackson's Lord of the Rings trilogy, green-lit by Shaye when every major studio had passed, is among the most financially successful and critically acclaimed film series in history: $2.9 billion box office, 17 Academy Awards including Best Picture for Return of the King. The decision to film all three simultaneously in New Zealand was unprecedented and risky. New Line's subsequent films failed to match this achievement, leading to merger with Warner Bros.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: New Line Cinema's green-lighting of the Lord of the Rings trilogy — which every major studio had rejected — resulted in 17 Academy Awards and $2.9 billion in box office revenue, the most consequential independent production decision in cinema history.
